sentences.text: Simosaurus was a marine reptile that grew to between 3 and 4 meters long. It possessed a blunt, flattened head featuring large upper temporal fossae located behind the eyes. The jaw joint was positioned far back, extending beyond the main part of the skull.
Unlike other nothosaurs, Simosaurus had blunt teeth likely adapted for crushing hard-shelled prey.
Simosaurus uniquely combined muscles for rapid jaw snapping with muscles providing crushing power at the rear of the jaw.
Fossil evidence suggests it fed on moderately hard-shelled organisms including Ceratites ammonites and holostean fish.

The first fossils of Simosaurus were discovered in Lunéville, France. A complete skull was found and sent to the German paleontologist Christian Erich Hermann von Meyer in 1842. He named the type species Simosaurus gaillardoti that year.

Simosaurus had a dorsoventrally flattened trunk and well-developed vertebrae that restricted side-to-side swimming movements. It likely generated most of its swimming thrust through a powerful downstroke of its forelimbs, indicated by well-developed humeral crests and a large pectoral girdle. Researchers consider it a moderately powerful swimmer with a locomotion style transitional between early sauropterygian undulation and plesiosaur flipper-driven swimming.

Simosaurus is often considered a durophagous reptile that fed on organisms with hard shells due to its blunt teeth. It possessed a long jaw structure resembling that of reptiles capable of snapping bites.
Simosaurus belongs to the family Simosauridae and is classified within the class Reptilia.

Simosaurus fossils found in France and Germany date back approximately 230 million years to the Middle Triassic period. Fossils from France originate from the upper Muschelkalk formation of the Ladinian stage in the Middle Triassic. The animal first appears in the nodosus biozone, characterized by abundant fossils of the ammonite Ceratites nodosus.
There is debate regarding the classification of Simosaurus, with some researchers considering it a pachypleurosaur or a primitive sauropterygian rather than a nothosaur.
